source: Publisher documentation saved under e3/truth/docs/fresh/ (sha256 in SHA256SUMS): TPC-DS v3.2.0; LDBC SNB specification (v2.2.5-SNAPSHOT, Appendix D for the Interactive v1 legacy data sets); GTFS Schedule Reference; FAA ardata.pdf (5/8/2025); ABS ASGS Edition 3 web pages; SEC Financial Statement Data Sets; College Scorecard Field of Study documentation (October 2026) and data dictionary; EPA AirData FileFormats (v3.0.0); 2024 ACS PUMS data dictionary and Census regions and divisions; City of Chicago portal metadata (ijzp-q8t2, c7ck-438e); USDA FoodData Central download field descriptions (October 2020)
rule: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or nesting statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened.

instance.generator: public data fixed before download for the confirmatory evaluation, joined by fresh.py
instance.construction: Auckland Transport static GTFS feed (gtfs.at.govt.nz/gtfs.zip), the snapshot downloaded for the confirmatory evaluation (date in the README), read against the GTFS Schedule Reference saved on 2026-10-27: stop_times (root, sampled to 1,000,000 records if larger) left-joined to trips on trip_id, routes on route_id, agency on agency_id, stops on stop_id and stops again (role parent) on parent_station; dropped stops.location_type (documented to be 0 or empty for every stop that stop_times references), agency_timezone (documented to be the same for all agencies), the free-text, URL, colour, accessibility and on-demand fields (stop_headsign, timepoint, continuous_*, *_booking_rule_id, stop_desc, stop_url, zone_id, stop_timezone, wheelchair_*, level_id, platform_code, route_desc, route_url, route_color, route_text_color, route_sort_order, trip_short_name, bikes_allowed, agency_url, agency_lang, agency_phone, agency_fare_url) to stay within 25 columns.

cleaning.missing_values: empty and missing references become '?', kept as a value (null = null)

truth.clause: gtfs_schedule_reference.html, Field Definitions, stop_times.txt: "Primary key (trip_id, stop_sequence)"; gtfs_schedule_reference.html, Dataset Attributes: "The primary key of a dataset is the field or combination of fields that uniquely identify a row."
truth.justification: (trip_id, stop_sequence) is the declared primary key of stop_times.txt; the documented 'A stop may be serviced multiple times in the same trip' rules out (trip_id, stop_id) -> stop_sequence.

audit.quote: Primary key (trip_id, stop_sequence) | The primary key of a dataset is the field or combination of fields that uniquely identify a row.
audit.source: gtfs_schedule_reference.html, Field Definitions, stop_times.txt; gtfs_schedule_reference.html, Dataset Attributes

truth.justification: trip_id references the primary key of trips.txt, whose row holds these fields; 'A block_id may have trips with different service days' rules out block_id -> service_id.

audit.quote: Primary key (trip_id) | trip_id: Foreign ID referencing trips.trip_id | The primary key of a dataset is the field or combination of fields that uniquely identify a row.

mined.algorithm: fdmine.py: exact discovery of all minimal FDs in the style of HyFD (no HyFD binary was available); the complete set of minimal FDs is unique, so it equals HyFD's output
